children: Middle East-linked air-cargo routes remain under pressure even as global freight demand continues to grow, the International Air Transport Association says. Global cargo demand rose 3.9% on year in July, but traffic on the Europe-Middle East corridor fell 16.1% and Middle East-Asia volumes dropped 14.1%, marking a fifth consecutive month of contraction for both routes. Middle Eastern carriers overall recorded 1.7% demand growth while capacity increased 4%. Higher fuel prices and geopolitical tensions remain risks to the global cargo outlook, IATA says.
